CausalChain: Iron overload/injury -> Increased ROS production -> Lipid peroxidation -> Impaired cystine uptake -> Decreased GSH synthesis -> Activation of iron-dependent ferroptosis -> Hepatocyte injury and liver disease progression -> CRISPRa-mediated upregulation of CBS/CGL -> Augmented cysteine synthesis -> Enhanced GSH biosynthesis -> Increased GPX4 activity -> Reduced lipid peroxidation -> Inhibition of ferroptosis; concurrently, targeted nanoparticle delivery and PNO1-mediated autophagy modulation + iron chelation further reinforce the pathway interruption.
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that a combinatorial therapeutic strategy, which leverages CRISPR/Cas9-based activation (CRISPRa) to upregulate the transsulfuration enzymes CBS and CGL in hepatocytes, can effectively compensate for impaired cystine uptake and restore glutathione homeostasis. This gene-editing approach, when delivered precisely via next-generation nanoparticle systems and augmented with targeted iron chelation and PNO1-mediated autophagy modulation, will increase endogenous cysteine availability, thereby enhancing GSH synthesis and sustaining GPX4 activity. The anticipated result is a significant reduction in ROS-induced lipid peroxidation and the subsequent inhibition of iron-dependent ferroptosis, ultimately protecting hepatocytes from injury in NASH and delaying the progression to fibrosis and HCC.
Abstract: We propose a multifaceted intervention that integrates CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene activation with advanced nanoparticle delivery systems and iron chelation to combat hepatocyte ferroptosis in non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). Building upon the established causal chain wherein iron overload leads to increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, triggering lipid peroxidation and impaired cystine uptake that culminates in reduced glutathione (GSH) synthesis and subsequent ferroptosis, our approach aims to restore redox balance. By specifically activating the transsulfuration pathway enzymes cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) and cystathionine γ-lyase (CGL) via CRISPRa, we intend to augment endogenous cysteine production, bolstering GSH biosynthesis and preserving GPX4 function. In parallel, we will employ targeted nanoparticles for precise delivery and incorporate modulation of autophagy, particularly through the PNO1 axis, to synergistically reduce lipid peroxidation. Furthermore, integration of iron chelation addresses the upstream burden of iron overload, ensuring a comprehensive blockade of the ferroptotic cascade. This integrated strategy is designed not only to protect hepatocytes from oxidative injury but also to delay the progression towards fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis focused primarily on CRISPR/Cas9-mediated activation of CBS and CGL through nanoparticle delivery to overcome impaired cystine uptake and restore GSH synthesis. In the revised hypothesis, we have incorporated additional layers reflective of current evidence: (1) Addressing upstream iron overload with iron chelation to reduce ROS production, (2) Explicitly modulating autophagy via the PNO1 pathway to offer a synergistic reduction in lipid peroxidation, and (3) Integrating advanced nanoparticle delivery systems that enhance precision and practical implementability. Each step of the original causal chain is maintained—iron overload to ROS, lipid peroxidation, decreased GSH, and ferroptosis—while our new proposal offers a more holistic, technology-enhanced strategy that targets multiple points within this cascade, thereby reinforcing both the novelty and feasibility of the approach.
